reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) confirms that rapid cooling via melt-spinning produces an amorphous structure in the alloy, but it does not provide any data on substrate thermal conductivity, cooling uniformity, residual stresses, or their effect on crystallization during reheating. The key premises about substrate optimization and its mechanism are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Enhanced substrate cooling uniformity minimizes local thermal gradients and residual stresses that serve as nucleation sites for crystallization during reheating.
A superior cooling substrate promotes a homogeneously amorphous, kinetically trapped state by reducing spatial variations in cooling.
Limiting the formation of crystalline precursors during cooling will reduce crystallization events during subsequent heating.
Melt-spun ribbons fabricated using the enhanced substrate will exhibit a higher amorphous fraction compared to those produced on conventional copper plates.
